title: DICTIONARY DWG item wire code is independent of hardOwner
scope: Correct and verify DICTIONARY item-handle parsing and encoding without changing the separate DXF group-code ownership policy. This closes a bounded DWG field-role defect only; no document-output or semantic support claim is promoted.

normativeSource.title: Open Design Specification for .dwg files v5.4.1
normativeSource.finding: The section identifies DICTIONARY itemhandles as soft owner references. Its hardOwner flag is a separate body field.

sourceRules: The DWG object decoder/encoder uses HANDLE_VECTOR_N(itemhandles, numitems, 2, 0), encoding dictionary itemhandles with wire code 2.
The DXF writer separately derives group 350 or 360 from hardOwner and recognizes special hard-owner dictionary keys.

observations: Handle 0xE8 has hardOwner=1 and ACAD_LAYERSTATES item tuple [2,1,233,233].
Handle 0x2CD has hardOwner=1 and ACAD_SORTENTS item tuple [2,2,718,718].

physicalSource.priorDisposition: The two DICTIONARY records at handles 0xE8 and 0x2CD failed parsing because the parser required a code-3 item when hardOwner=1.
physicalSource.currentDisposition: Both records parse with one complete item each; DWG read observations report objectParseFailures=0. The named-block SORTENTSTABLE owner remains outside the qualified DXF owner scope.

behavior: The parser and writer use DWG soft-owner code 2 for every non-null DICTIONARY item handle, independent of hardOwner.
hardOwner remains available to the DXF layer for group-350/group-360 ownership policy.
The existing dwgItemHandleCode API is retained; only its role mapping changed.

coverage: Exact emitted item wire code is 2 for both hardOwner values across all six supported DWG writer revisions.
Generated AC1024 frames parse code-2 items with hardOwner=0 and hardOwner=1 and preserve a following sentinel handle.
Generated code-3 item handles are rejected for either flag and partial typed entries are cleared.

dxfOwnershipCompatibility.coverage: Existing generated custom-owner DICTIONARYVAR graphs preserve entry ownership and typed values through DXF import/output; this confirms the separate DXF group-role path remains intact.

physicalTrace.result: DWG read completed with objectParseFailures=0; handles 0xE8 and 0x2CD each report one parsed dictionary entry. Strict DXF export remains refused at the independent DICTIONARYVAR source/output snapshot gate.

broaderAdapterAttempts.result: No output qualification: the current partial export retry is blocked by an unclosed FIELDLIST profile.
No output qualification: the current run is blocked by the DICTIONARYWDFLT import-receipt gate.

No new evidence accepted: the broader generated cohort currently fails at a typed DICTIONARYVAR readback condition after the ASCII hardOwner group-code and owner-closure checks; the binary hardOwner case was not reached.

limitations: The physical AC1018 file is inspected locally and is not added as a repository fixture.
No full physical DWG-to-DXF output/readback or native application acceptance is established by this correction.
The AC1018 named-block SORTENTSTABLE dictionary/table graph remains refused under the existing DXF owner-scope rule.
DXF 350/360 ownership behavior remains a separate projection and is not changed by the DWG item wire-code correction.

supersedes.scope: Its general statement that DWG item-handle wire role follows hardOwner and its hardOwner=1/code-3 generated vector. The AC1024 hardOwner=0 ACAD_SUN physical observation and bounded group-350 DXF output evidence remain valid.

nextAction: Continue P4 source/graph closure using the corrected per-field wire role. Keep named-block SORTENTSTABLE, empty-name STYLE, and other unclosed graphs refused until their independent owner and consumer gates pass.
